title: The hill becomes a roof
hookLine: Indra sends a storm to drown the village, and Krishna lifts the hill and calls everyone under it
carry: sharanagati: he shelters everyone who runs to him

lines: THE CLOUDS OF THE WORLD'S END.
cards: Indra is furious. The king of the gods has been passed over by a village of cowherds, on the advice of a child. So he calls up the clouds kept, the text says, for the end of the world, and sends them over Vraja.
The sky goes black. Rain comes down in torrents, with hail, lightning and a wind that knocks over everything standing. The cows shiver and shield their calves with their bodies.
The cowherds, soaked and terrified, gather around the boy who started all this. Krishna, protect us.

teach.b: Krishna looks at the storm and understands it. This is Indra's pride, he thinks, and the people who depend on me are in danger because of it. So he walks to the hill, Govardhan, and lifts it.
The Bhagavata's picture is wonderfully small: he holds it up as easily as a child holds up a mushroom.
Come under, he calls. Bring your cows, your carts, your families. Don't be afraid it will fall.
And the whole village comes in under the hill, out of the rain. He holds it up for seven days, the text says, without moving, not hungry, not thirsty. Outside, Indra pours down everything he has.
Under the hill, nothing reaches them. At last Indra, astonished, lets his pride give way and calls the clouds back. Krishna sets the hill back exactly where it was.

teach.h: GIRIDHARI: REFUGE FOR ALL WHO COME.
teach.b: This is why one of Krishna's best-loved names is Giridhari, the one who holds up the hill; the poet-saint Mirabai sang to him by that name. The teaching under it is refuge, sharanagati. The village did nothing clever.
They ran to him, and he made room for every one of them, cows and carts included.
Look back at the week: a mother given the grace to love him, a serpent sheltered by his feet, a village that fed the hill, and now the hill held over them all.

how: Krishna as Giridhari, the one who holds up the hill, is a familiar name and image in Hindu devotion, and on Govardhan Puja some communities build a small hill of food and offer it in memory of this story.

o: the hill that Indra hurls down onto the village
the boy holding up the hill so all can shelter
the flood that rises over the fields of Vraja

games.q: the storm and the hill — tap the pairs.
p: sends the clouds of the world's end
how easily a child holds it up

s: Krishna fights Indra in the sky
he doesn't fight. he lifts the hill and holds it as shelter until Indra gives up.
the text says he held the hill for seven days
without moving, without hunger or thirst.
afterward the hill is left floating
he sets it back exactly where it was.

games.q: you're Krishna. Indra's storm is drowning the village, and everyone has turned to you. what do you do?
o: send a storm back at Indra.
lift the hill and call everyone under it.
lead the village away to another valley.
games.why: he lifts Govardhan with one hand, like a child holding a mushroom, and shelters them all. that's why he's called Giridhari.

practice: In the Pushti Marg tradition, devotees repeat a short prayer of refuge: Shri Krishna sharanam mama, Krishna is my refuge. Breathe in. Breathing out, say it softly, or in English: Krishna, you are my refuge.
Let a storm in your life come to mind, and picture yourself coming in under the hill. Then think of someone who might need to come in under your roof this week.
If you don't pray, remember a time something sheltered you, breathe in that dry, safe air, and hold that person there with you.

wordCard.voice: Govardhan lifted. A boy raises the hill on one hand, and a whole village and its cows shelter beneath it while the storm rages.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Govardhana, the hill near Vraja that Krishna lifted.

carryVoice: Your line: sharanagati: he shelters everyone who runs to him. Tomorrow, a flute in the trees. Day eight hundred ninety-six: a week, done.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.25, Indra's storm, the lifting of Govardhan, the seven days, and Indra's withdrawal
